sections.html:
Blair County's Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds work out of one office in the courthouse at 423 Allegheny Street, Suite 145, Hollidaysburg, PA 16648. The phone is (814) 693-3095. Doors are open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed on legal holidays, and staff stay through lunch.

Land records here start in 1846, the year the county was carved out of Huntingdon and Bedford counties. Recorded documents are public and anyone can view them during business hours. The one exception is military discharge papers, which are impounded. You can also search remotely through Landex. A free Record Alert service will text or email you when something is recorded under up to five names you sign up.

A deed costs $87.75, and a mortgage costs the same. That price covers up to four names and four pages. Each extra name adds $0.50 and each extra page adds $2.00. Make checks payable to Blair County Recorder of Deeds. The office takes no credit cards.

Blair County recording fees

Recording a military discharge, and certified copies of it, is free. For any document without a listed price, the Recorder sets the fee.

Three rules catch a lot of filers. A deed that claims an exemption from realty transfer tax needs two statements of value. Every deed, mortgage and assignment needs a signed certificate of residence with the exact address of the grantee, mortgagee or assignee. And blanket assignments, releases and satisfactions are turned away.

  • Include a self-addressed, stamped envelope, sized right for the return.
  • Name the correct municipality and mark it as a city, township or borough.
  • Awards of real estate and decrees of distribution go in with a statement of value.
  • A lease of 30 years or more is $59.75 and needs a statement of value. Shorter leases are $18.50.

Before you pick a net figure, ask the Recorder at (814) 693-3095, or your closing agent, which transfer tax rate applies in your municipality and school district.

sections.h2: What time to turn in a deed
sections.html:
Get your documents in by 3:15 p.m. Anything submitted after that may not be processed the same day. The recording desk itself stays open until 3:45 p.m., but if you need a same-day record for a closing, the earlier cutoff is the one to plan around.

You can skip the trip with e-recording. The office accepts filings through Simplifile, CSC at eRecording.com and ePN, and the county pitches it as a way to save time, postage and checks. Mail and counter drop-off work too, provided the return envelope is in the package.

The office posts a holiday calendar. For the rest of 2026 it shows closures on Thanksgiving, the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, so schedule a closing near those dates with that in mind.

Blair County covers 527 square miles around Altoona, with Hollidaysburg as the county seat. Population was estimated at 119,541 in 2025, a 2.7% slide since 2020. The county counts 56,086 housing units and 50,558 households, with 72.4% of homes lived in by their owners. The median value of an owner-occupied home for 2020 to 2024 was $161,100, and median gross rent was $885. Builders pulled just 86 permits in 2025, so a resale rarely competes with new homes. Roughly 24.5% of residents are 65 or older. Buyers touring an older house tend to scrutinize the roof and furnace.

Deeds and mortgages are only part of what gets filed here. Agreements, affidavits, bills of sale, powers of attorney, ordinances, waivers and sewage permits are $18.50 each. Articles of agreement, installment sales agreements, declarations of taking and notices of condemnation are $59.75. An order of court is $20.50.

  • Subdivision plans cost $30.00 for page one, then $10.00 per added page.
  • Surveys and plans cost $10.00 for page one, then $5.00 per added page.
  • Highway plans cost $18.00 for page one, then $3.00 per added page.
  • UCC financing statements: $100.00.
  • Notary public bond, oath and commission: $38.50.

A satisfaction by order of court is $64.75, the same as an ordinary satisfaction piece. If you hold a paid-off mortgage that was never released, the satisfaction is the filing that clears it from the index before you sell.

No photography is allowed in the office, and that covers phones, so bring paper and a pen when you look up a record. Staff give general information by phone but won't search records or offer legal advice. For anything deeper, hire a title examiner or an attorney.

Plan your visit around the cutoff times and document rules above. Bring a check, since cards are refused, and a stamped, self-addressed envelope for any mailed or dropped-off filing. A family transfer that claims a tax exemption needs two statements of value, so it takes more prep than an ordinary arm's length sale.

sections.h2: Getting a copy of your deed
sections.html:
Landex has records online. Or walk in during business hours and staff will locate the reference and photocopy it for you. Counter copies run 25 cents a page. If you ask by mail, email or fax, give the full name, the property location and the year of purchase. Those cost $1.00 per page, and you supply a stamped, self-addressed return envelope. Certifying a copy adds $2.00.

A certified copy can stand in for a lost or destroyed deed. A recorded document can't be altered after the fact. To add, drop or change a name, record a new deed. Office staff can't prepare deeds, so an attorney drafts it. When a spouse dies and the couple held title as tenants by the entireties, the name normally can stay on until the house is sold or mortgaged. The next deed then records the date of death.

sections.h2: Recording a deed, step by step
sections.html: An attorney or your closing agent drafts the deed. Clip on the signed certificate of residence, plus both statements of value if you claim an exemption. Cut a check for the fee and enclose a return envelope with postage so the original finds its way back to the buyer. Pick how it travels: e-recording vendor, post, or the counter before 3:15 p.m. If a payoff is part of the sale, confirm with your closing agent that the release or satisfaction gets filed, because that wipes the old lien from the index.

faqs.q: How much is a deed recording fee in Blair County?
faqs.a: It is $87.75 for a deed with up to four names and four pages. Each extra name costs $0.50 and each extra page costs $2.00.

faqs.q: Does the Blair County Recorder of Deeds take credit cards?
faqs.a: No. Pay by check made out to Blair County Recorder of Deeds.

faqs.q: Can a Blair County deed be recorded electronically?
faqs.a: Yes. The office accepts e-recording through Simplifile, CSC at eRecording.com and ePN.

faqs.q: What certificate of residence does a Blair County deed need?
faqs.a: Every deed, mortgage and assignment needs a signed certificate of residence with the exact address of the grantee, mortgagee or assignee.

faqs.q: How do I find the earliest Blair County records?
faqs.a: Records start in 1846, when the county was formed from Huntingdon and Bedford counties. Search them online through Landex or visit the office in Hollidaysburg.
